topic.subject: science
topic.title: Crop production and management
topic.scope: kharif and rabi crops, soil preparation, sowing, manure and fertilisers, irrigation, weeding, harvesting, storage

misconceptions.statement: All crops are grown throughout the year regardless of the season.
misconceptions.why: Students observe vegetables in the market year-round and assume they are grown locally at all times.
misconceptions.fix: Crops have specific requirements for temperature, humidity, and rainfall, leading to distinct Kharif and Rabi seasons.

probe.question: Can we grow wheat in the middle of the rainy season in India?
probe.wrong_answer: Yes, because crops can grow whenever we plant them.

misconceptions.statement: Ploughing is done only to remove weeds.
misconceptions.why: Students see farmers removing weeds during field preparation and assume that is the sole purpose.
misconceptions.fix: Ploughing also loosens the soil, allowing roots to penetrate deeper and improving aeration for soil microbes.

probe.question: Why do farmers loosen the soil before sowing seeds?
probe.wrong_answer: To get rid of the weeds so they don't steal the space.

misconceptions.statement: Fertilisers are better than manure because they are man-made and more powerful.
misconceptions.why: The word 'fertiliser' sounds more scientific and 'manure' is associated with waste, leading to a bias toward industrial products.
misconceptions.fix: Manure improves soil texture and water-holding capacity, whereas fertilisers provide specific nutrients but can harm soil health if overused.

probe.question: Which is better for long-term soil health: chemical fertilisers or organic manure?
probe.wrong_answer: Fertilisers, because they are made in factories to be stronger and faster.

misconceptions.statement: Plants need water only when they look wilted.
misconceptions.why: Students equate plant health with visible turgidity, ignoring the need for constant moisture for nutrient uptake.
misconceptions.fix: Irrigation must be provided at regular intervals based on the crop's growth stage and soil type, not just when visible wilting occurs.

probe.question: Should a farmer wait for the leaves to droop before watering the field?
probe.wrong_answer: Yes, that is the best way to know the plant is thirsty.
